test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?

options.text: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit

solution:
The correct answer is __**Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indirect transmission refers to the transfer of infectious agents to a susceptible person through a contaminated intermediate object or organism.
 
• The five Fs of indirect transmission are: **Flies, fingers, fomites, food, and fluid**.
 
• These five Fs represent the common pathways through which pathogens can be transmitted indirectly.
 
• Understanding these pathways is crucial in implementing effective infection control measures to prevent the spread of diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flies**: Flies can act as vectors by carrying pathogens on their bodies and contaminating food or surfaces they land on.
 
• **Fingers**: Hands can become contaminated through contact with infected surfaces, body fluids, or during the handling of contaminated objects, leading to the spread of pathogens.
 
• **Fomites**: Fomites are inanimate objects like doorknobs, utensils, or clothing that can harbor infectious agents and facilitate their transmission when touched by individuals.
 
• **Food**: Contaminated food can be a source of infection if it is prepared, handled, or stored improperly, allowing pathogens to multiply and cause illness.
 
• **Fluid**: Contaminated water or other fluids can serve as a medium for the transmission of pathogens, especially in areas with poor sanitation and hygiene practices.
